items.title: chinamobile, chinatelecom, chinabroadnet: add 3GPP public domains
items.body:
## Background

`category-ru` already lists `mcc250.pub.3gppnetwork.org` (Mobile IMS) for Russian operators, but there is no equivalent for mainland China operators. To find out which mainland operators actually hold a delegation under `pub.3gppnetwork.org`, I ran a full NS scan of `mnc000` – `mnc999` under both `mcc460` and `mcc461`.

Note: every name under `mccXXX.pub.3gppnetwork.org` returns `NOERROR` even when nothing is delegated there, so only names that return actual NS records are counted as delegated.

## Scan results

| Operator | Delegated zone | NS servers | NS ASN |
|---|---|---|---|
| China Mobile | `mnc000.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` | `ns.cnmobile.net`, `ns2.cnmobile.net`, `ns1.cmmobile.cn`, `ns2.cmmobile.cn` | AS9808 |
| China Mobile | `mnc002.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` | same as above | AS9808 |
| China Mobile | `mnc004.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` | same as above | AS9808 |
| China Mobile | `mnc007.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` | same as above | AS9808 |
| China Telecom | `mnc011.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` | `ns1.chinanet.cn`, `ns2.chinanet.cn`, `ns3.chinanet.cn` | AS4134 |
| China Broadnet | `mnc015.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` | `vip3.alidns.com`, `vip4.alidns.com` (Alibaba Cloud DNS) | AS45102 |

- No delegation exists for any other MNC under `mcc460` (including China Unicom's `001` / `006` / `009`), or for any MNC under `mcc461`.
- Each zone's SOA is served authoritatively by the NS servers listed above, so the delegations are live, not lame.
- The results are identical across Google / Cloudflare DoH (queried from outside China) and `223.5.5.5`, `119.29.29.29`, `202.103.224.68` (queried over UDP 53 from inside China).

## ePDG

`epdg.epc.mncXXX.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` returns `NXDOMAIN` (A and AAAA) for all 6 delegated MNCs, answered authoritatively by each operator's own NS. It is not known whether these operators publish any other records in these zones besides ePDG.

## Why no `@!cn`

This PR is not the usual case of "the domain belongs to a mainland China company and resolves to mainland China IPs": the parent domain is managed by 3GPP, and the ePDG names currently return `NXDOMAIN`. Still, these subdomains are delegated to the name servers of mainland China ISPs, and they will very likely only ever be used for those operators' domestic services. They are therefore added without `@!cn`, and end up in `geolocation-cn` through the operator lists.

## Changes

- `chinamobile`: `mnc000`, `mnc002`, `mnc004`, `mnc007` `.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org`
- `chinatelecom`: `mnc011.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org`
- `chinabroadnet`: `mnc015.mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org`

## Open question: add `mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` as a whole?

I'm not sure whether `mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` itself should also be added to the cn lists (e.g. `geolocation-cn`, which `geosite:cn` includes), the same way `category-ru` lists `mcc250.pub.3gppnetwork.org`. Virtually every subdomain under it is bound to be delegated to a mainland China ISP, so adding it to the cn lists seems reasonable.

It would also cover future delegations. If China Unicom later registers a delegation of its own, or a new operator appears in mainland China, that operator's `pub.3gppnetwork.org` zone would not match any list generated by this project under the per-MNC approach in this PR. Adding `mcc460.pub.3gppnetwork.org` to the cn lists avoids that problem.

If you have any thoughts on this, I'm happy to revise the PR further.
